description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:102-107

```rust
fn blob_exists(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    blob_id: &jmap_types::Id,
) -> impl std::future::Future<Output = bool> + Send;
```

The signature returns `bool`, not `Result<bool, Self::Error>`. A backend
implementor whose blob store is a remote service (S3, GridFS, sftp) cannot
distinguish three states that the caller actually needs to distinguish:

1. "Definitely not there" (blob never uploaded)
2. "Definitely there" (blob present and reachable)
3. "I don't know — connectivity failed"

State 3 has no representation. The implementor must choose:
- Return `false` on transient errors → creates produce a misleading
  `invalidProperties: blob not found` SetError when the blob *might*
  exist; the client will retry with the same `blobId` and the operation
  will succeed once the backend reconnects. Data is not lost but the
  client receives a wrong-shape error.
- Return `true` on transient errors → creates proceed; then
  `create_object` fails downstream with a different error, possibly
  after partial state mutation, and the client sees an internally
  inconsistent response.
- Panic → caller sees `serverFail` but with no actionable diagnostic.

The handler in src/filenode.rs:434 calls `!backend.blob_exists(...)`
and immediately emits `invalidProperties` with description "blob not
found". That description is a lie when the backend is unreachable.

Contract for a caller depending on this in production: there is no
correct implementation. A database-backed backend must pick a
silent-wrong-result behaviour.

Propagation note: canonical sibling `MailBackend::blob_exists`
(crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:188) has the same signature.
Per the workspace canonical-template rule, fix mail-server first
then propagate. The mail-server docstring explicitly mentions the
"distinguish two failure cases" requirement for RFC 8621 §5.8 but
its own signature does not let the backend signal the third case
(transient unreachability). Both crates need the same widening to
`Result<bool, Self::Error>`.

Suggested fix: change to `Result<bool, Self::Error>`, then the
handler maps `Err` → `serverFail` (transient/retryable) and `Ok(false)`
→ `invalidProperties: blob not found` (deterministic).
title: FileNodeBackend::blob_exists returns bool, conflating 'not found' with 'backend unreachable'
